clue.text: Muslim ruler's last month in hospital

indicators.note: in places the word for last month inside the word for hospital

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital
ULT is short for ultimo, an old business word for last month

explanation.surface: A ruler's final month is spent in a hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is the sovereign of an Islamic state, such as Oman or Brunei.

clue.text: Private soldier, second one of four to go west

parts.note: a quad is one of quadruplets, one of four
to go west is an idiom meaning to die

explanation.surface: A soldier is one of four sent off westwards.
explanation.walkthrough: A squaddie is British slang for an ordinary soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a squaddie is a private, the lowest army rank.

clue.text: No-hoper's new role picking up seaweed at front

indicators.note: picking up has the rearranged letters take in another letter
new signals that the letters of role are rearranged
at front asks for the opening letter of seaweed

explanation.surface: A useless person's fresh job involves collecting seaweed on the seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ROLE into LOER, which takes in S. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who habitually fails, a hopeless case.

clue.text: Area north of Italian islet

indicators.note: in a down clue north of puts one piece above the other

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A region north of Italy forms a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: An ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames.

clue.text: Unmannerly chit initially having fling with one's husband

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of chit

parts.note: to fling is to hurl
one is I, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: A rude young girl is having an affair with somebody's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' looks like a romantic affair but is the verb throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Churlish behaviour is rude and boorish, a synonym for lacking manners.

clue.text: Doctor's alter ego trapping rodent in compound

indicators.note: trapping has the alter ego surround the rodent

parts.note: Mr Hyde is Dr Jekyll's alter ego in Stevenson's story
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: Jekyll's dark side captures a rat inside a walled enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' is a chemical, not an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrate is a chemical substance containing combined water.

clue.text: Approved play area old firm finally repaired

parts.note: a rec, recreation ground, is a play area

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of firm

parts.note: mended means repaired

explanation.surface: A playground for an old company was finally fixed and signed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recommended has been endorsed or commended as suitable.

clue.text: Popular countertenor once going about with one persistently present

parts.note: IN means popular

indicators.note: going about has the singer's name surround the letter for with

parts.note: Alfred Deller was a celebrated English countertenor of the past century

explanation.surface: A well-liked singer of old tours with somebody who never goes away.
explanation.definitionFit: An indweller is one who dwells within, an inhabitant always present.

clue.text: Sound made by animal, male, beginning to eat fruit

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of eat

parts.note: a haw is the fruit of the hawthorn

explanation.surface: A male animal makes a noise as it starts eating fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hee-haw is the bray of a donkey.

clue.text: Irish county's leader absent constantly

indicators.note: leader absent means the county name loses its first letter

parts.note: Galway is a county in the west of Ireland, so county's gives GALWAYS

explanation.surface: An Irish county's chief is forever away.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means at all times, without exception.

clue.text: Outstanding peacekeepers put down roots

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces belong to the United Nations
to put down roots somewhere is to have settled there

explanation.surface: Remarkable peacekeeping troops have made a permanent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means not yet paid or resolved, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding bill or dispute is still pending, so it remains unresolved.

clue.text: Military unit's chaplain quietly becoming Conservative

indicators.note: becoming shows the letter for quietly turning into the letter for Conservative

parts.note: a padre is a military chaplain
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: An army chaplain quietly switches his politics to the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of officers or trained personnel forming a military nucleus.

clue.text: Tanzanian port makes bold sadly to back America

parts.note: to make bold to do something is to dare, so makes bold is DARES

indicators.note: back means the word for sadly is read from right to left

parts.note: alas is an exclamation said sadly

explanation.surface: Someone grows sadly brave in order to support the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Dar es Salaam is the largest city and main harbour of Tanzania on the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Sea cook's story verbally identifying worker in precious metal

parts.note: Long John Silver is the ship's cook in Treasure Island

indicators.note: verbally means the word for story is taken as spoken

parts.note: a myth is a story

explanation.surface: A ship's cook tells a tale that reveals a metalworker.
explanation.walkthrough: SILVER'S plus MITH, which sounds like 'myth' ('verbally').
explanation.definitionFit: A silversmith crafts objects from silver, a precious metal.

clue.text: Continental character, and when he might turn up?

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet, from the European continent

explanation.surface: A European figure and the moment he is expected to show.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh Greek letter; ETA also gives an arrival time for a visitor.

clue.text: Sources of comfort only found lining fashionable shoes at first

indicators.note: found lining means the word for only sits inside, like a lining, the other letters

parts.note: IN means fashionable

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of shoes

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: The only comfort is found in the lining of trendy shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found lining' is the container signal: the 'only' word forms the lining between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Insoles are cushioned inner soles placed in shoes to make walking more comfortable.

clue.text: Onlooker's cheers welcomed by policeman dropping in

indicators.note: welcomed by has the thanks word taken into the shortened rank
dropping means the letters of in are lost from the officer's rank

parts.note: an inspector is a police officer
ta and cheers both mean thanks

explanation.surface: A police officer calling in is greeted with cheers by a bystander.
explanation.walkthrough: INSPECTOR loses IN ('dropping'), leaving SPECTOR, which takes in TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator watches an event, an onlooker.

clue.text: See Anglican cleric entering calmly

indicators.note: entering puts the cleric inside the word for See

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
Ven, Venerable, is the title of an Anglican archdeacon

explanation.surface: Watch a Church of England clergyman walking in serenely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: To act evenly is to do so steadily and without agitation.

clue.text: Like Rumpole we lay drunk on railway

indicators.note: drunk signals the letters of we lay are shaken up

explanation.surface: Imitating a famous barrister, we lay intoxicated on the tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpole of the Bailey is a fictional London barrister from British TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawyerly means characteristic of a lawyer, as the barrister Rumpole is.

clue.text: Aim to follow member's story

indicators.note: to follow puts the word for aim after the limb

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A goal to pursue a club member's tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale, often of uncertain truth.

clue.text: Gap traversed by the German fishing-boat

indicators.note: traversed by has the German article spanning the gap

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a rift is a gap

explanation.surface: A German boat crosses a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a fishing vessel that uses drift nets.

clue.text: A northern girl crossing river in mountainous principality

indicators.note: crossing has the girl's name spanning the river letter

parts.note: Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from the north wades a river in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a small Pyrenean principality between France and Spain.

clue.text: Tree-lined approach, a place to meet

parts.note: a venue is a place for meeting

explanation.surface: A tree-lined approach is a good spot to meet up.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a double definition, but 'a' is A and 'place to meet' VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad road, often lined with trees, leading to a house.

clue.text: Extreme characters crushing a meadow plant

indicators.note: crushing in a down clue has the extreme letters sit on top of, pressing down on, the rest

parts.note: A and Z are the first and last letters of the alphabet
a lea is a meadow

explanation.surface: Letters at the edges squash a plant in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: An azalea is a flowering shrub of the rhododendron family.

clue.text: Spot head of zoo taking computer studies

indicators.note: head of asks for the opening letter of zoo

parts.note: IT, information technology, is the study of computing

explanation.surface: Notice the zoo's director signing up for a computing course.
explanation.definitionFit: A zit is slang for a pimple, a spot on the skin.

clue.text: Way I write journal, like some magistrates

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
to pen is to write
a diary is a journal

explanation.surface: A description of how one person writes a daily journal, compared with magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipendiary magistrates are salaried legal professionals, unlike unpaid lay justices.

clue.text: Big lorry, one originally carrying paintings on top

indicators.note: on top puts the word for paintings above the rest in this down clue

parts.note: art means paintings
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letter of carrying

explanation.surface: A huge truck has paintings stacked on its roof.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a tractor-trailer truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Artic is short for articulated lorry, a large truck.

clue.text: In Bhopal, a thick, long, heavy stick

indicators.note: In tells us the answer lies inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: In an Indian city, a thick heavy stick is carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is an Indian iron-bound bamboo staff used by police; Bhopal is an Indian city.

clue.text: Musician, odd chap associated with tango

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rum means odd or strange
Peter is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A musician is a strange fellow linked to a Latin dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter is a player of the trumpet, a brass musician.

clue.text: American writer needing oxygen in gym

indicators.note: in places the oxygen symbol inside the gym letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is gym class
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A US author needs some fresh air in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author of macabre tales.

clue.text: A year's rent for an old place in Scotland

parts.note: YR is the abbreviation for year, so year's gives YRS
to rent something is to hire it

explanation.surface: A twelve-month lease on a historic Scottish property.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayrshire is a former county of south-west Scotland, hence 'old place'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayrshire was a Scottish county until local government reorganisation abolished it.

clue.text: Make an impression in Turkey's borders, being irritable

indicators.note: in places the engraving word inside the other letters
borders asks for the first and last letters of Turkey

parts.note: to etch is to make an impression by engraving

explanation.surface: Someone cross trying to make an impact on Turkey's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey's borders' gives T and Y, around ETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy describes someone short-tempered and easily annoyed.
